title: DR drill automation: snapshot fingerprinting + SLO-gated traffic throttle
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements an automated active-passive DR drill that focuses on rapid snapshot validation and an SLO-gated traffic throttling experiment. Key ideas: generate cryptographic fingerprints of KV and metadata snapshots, exercise a synthetic ramped traffic profile against the passive region while exercising circuit-breaker hysteresis and load-shedding, and verify end-to-end restore fidelity and latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Validate that snapshot fingerprints (SHA256) produced in the primary match the artifacts used to rehydrate passive within 30 minutes.
- Verify KV rehydrate integrity using checksum and selective key sampling (target 99.99% key reconciliation).
- Ensure P95 generation latency in passive region remains below 150ms under low-medium load; P99 < 300ms during controlled ramp.
- Confirm circuit-breaker and load-shed policies trigger at configured thresholds and that automatic throttles (SLO-gated) reduce load without application-level errors >1%.
- Measure restore time and produce a Recovery Fingerprint report for audit.

Scope:
- Regions: us-west-2 (primary), eu-west-1 (passive).
- Services: tokenstore, request-router, runtime-gateway, kv-backend.
- Not in scope: long-term archival restore or cross-region DNS TTL changes outside orchestrator.

Success criteria (stop conditions):
- Passive region accepts rehydrated snapshots and KV checksum delta <= 0.01% for sampled key set.
- Dashboards show no more than 1% 5xx rate increase above baseline across services during drill.
- Recovery Fingerprint document generated and uploaded to Confluence (see attachments).

Prerequisites / Prechecks:
1) Verify backup snapshots exist for last 24 hours in s3://redwood-dr-snapshots/us-west-2 with manifest.
2) Ensure DR-runner job image is published: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/dr-tools:sha-20260301.
3) Circuit-breaker and load-shedding policies annotated in config repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/274.
4) Notify page and on-call: #oncall-drill, at least 48 hours notice given to customer-ops.

Automated Drill Steps (run by oncall or reliability eng runbook tool):
- Step A: Create Snapshot Fingerprint
  - On primary, run: ./scripts/dr-fingerprint.sh --prefix us-west-2 --out /tmp/fingerprint-usw2-$(date +%s).json
  - Fingerprint includes SHA256 of the snapshot files, key-hash sample stats, and manifest TTL.
  - Upload fingerprint to S3 and tag as drill-{date}.
  - Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/dr-tools/tree/main/scripts/dr-fingerprint.sh

- Step B: Trigger Passive Rehydrate (dry-run mode first)
  - Use orchestration API: POST /orchestrator/v1/rehydrate?region=eu-west-1&dry_run=true
  - Confirm rehydrate plan and estimated restore time. If estimated > 45 minutes, abort and investigate.
  - If dry-run OK, proceed to non-dry run: POST /orchestrator/v1/rehydrate?region=eu-west-1

- Step C: Start Synthetic Traffic Ramp (SLO-gated)
  - Launch dr-runner profile 'slo-ramp-3' from dr-tools. This profile ramps traffic 0->30% baseline over 10 minutes, then 30->60% if P95 < 150ms for 5 mins, otherwise it holds and triggers a lower ramp. The runner watches Grafana SLO queries and will back off automatically.
  - Command: dr-runner run --profile slo-ramp-3 --target eu-west-1 --watch-grafana https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/slo-dashboard

- Step D: Observe Circuit-breaker Behavior and Load-shedding
  - Circuit-breaker config: threshold 10% 5xx over 1m for runtime-gateway; hysteresis 2x cooldown.
  - If breaker opens, orchestration should redirect 50% of traffic to hosted fallback or serve limited tokens per-second. Confirm fallback metrics and capture time-to-open and time-to-close.

- Step E: KV Integrity Validation
  - Run checksum tool: ./tools/kv-compare --source s3://redwood-dr-snapshots/us-west-2/manifest.json --target eu-west-1 --sample-rate 0.001 --out report.csv
  - Expected: <0.01% mismatches; any mismatch triggers targeted rehydrate of affected key ranges.

- Step F: Smoke Tests and Rollback Plan
  - Run smoke-suite: gh pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/smoke-tests/pull/78
  - If smoke fails or SLO regressions exceed thresholds, run rollback: POST /orchestrator/v1/cancel-rehydrate?region=eu-west-1 & trigger failback plan tokenstore-rollback-2026-03.

- Step G: Recovery Fingerprint and Artifacts
  - On completion, generate recovery fingerprint with timings, checksums, and circuit-breaker events. Upload to Confluence and attach to this ticket.

Verification Queries / Dashboards:
- Grafana SLO panel: p95_generation_latency{region="eu-west-1"} and p99_generation_latency.
- Error budget burn: sum(rate(errors[5m])) / sum(rate(requests[5m])).
- KV reconciliation: SELECT count(1) as mismatches FROM kv_reconcile WHERE drill_tag='2026-03-10' AND mismatched=true;

Artifacts / Links:
- Confluence DR doc (template): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/DR+Drill+Template
- Orchestrator API spec: https://internal-api.redwood.ai/orchestrator/swagger
- Infra-config PR for circuit-breaker: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/274
- DR tools repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dr-tools
- Smoke tests PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/smoke-tests/pull/78

Roles & Owners:
- Drill lead: Liam O'Connor (assignee)
- Snapshot verification: Mei Chen
- KV integrity tooling: Diego Morales
- Monitoring & SLO analysis: Priya Nair
- Post-dr report and audit upload: Asha Patel

Post-dr Actions:
- Publish Recovery Fingerprint and attach to weekly reliability review.
- Create follow-up tickets for any mismatches with severity tags.
- Update circuit-breaker thresholds if we observed frequent false opens during controlled ramp.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Snapshot manifest corruption. Mitigation: validate SHA256 of manifest and keep redundant snapshot copies for 72 hours.
- Risk: Unexpected DNS propagation delay. Mitigation: use traffic router with explicit per-region routing rules (no global DNS change during drill).

Notes on uniqueness and experiments:
- This drill centralizes cryptographic snapshot fingerprinting and couples the traffic ramp to live SLO signals (instead of fixed time windows). The SLO-gated approach reduces blast radius and provides measurable feedback for policy tuning.
